first_impression.reaction: James googled 'honeymoon planner cost' on the train because if we go abroad for the wedding we'd want the honeymoon done by the same people, not something we sort out on spreadsheets at night. The title promises a cost and the first line tells us 'A number on its own tells you very little.' Fair enough, I'm a lawyer, I know 'it depends' is sometimes the honest answer, but it still feels like being told no before I've asked. What kept me reading was the bit about lining up flight arrivals with check-in times and transfers eating half a day. That's someone who's actually done it. The questions list and the fee-in-writing line are useful. No fairytale language, nothing tacky, no shouting. I'd skim the protection section, read the Wedded Wonderland bit and the FAQ, and send the questions list to James's mum, who's paying part of this.

journey.quote: A number on its own tells you very little.
journey.reaction: Honest, but the headline says 'Honeymoon Planner Cost' and I'm being told there's no number in the first paragraph. I understand why. It still stings a bit when you came for a figure.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: Someone has to compare options, read each supplier's terms, line up flight arrivals with check-in times, hold dates while you decide and confirm the small requests that make a stay feel considered: the late check-out, the dietary note, the quiet table on the last night.
journey.reaction: This is the answer to 'what does end-to-end actually mean' that every planner dodges. Exactly the evenings we don't want to spend.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: A planner who knows a region can tell you which island suits a slow week, which city works for three nights rather than five and where a transfer will eat half a day.
journey.reaction: Insider detail. Makes the fee feel like it pays for judgement, not admin.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: You give nothing up by handing the trip to someone else.
journey.reaction: Good to know, and not overclaimed. They're not pretending we're safer with them.

journey.section: The fee and the trip are two different costs
journey.quote: They move independently, and a clear quote shows each one separately.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful idea on the page. Hidden costs are my biggest worry, and asking for the fee and the trip to be shown separately is something I can actually hold a planner to.

journey.section: What moves the cost of the trip
journey.quote: None of these is right or wrong. They are simply where your choices show up on the quote.
journey.reaction: Clear, but these levers are fairly obvious. Season and length cost more, yes. Not the part I'd forward to anyone.

journey.section: How planners may charge, as questions to ask
journey.quote: Do you receive commissions from the suppliers you book, and will you tell us which?
journey.reaction: Good that it's on the list. Now I want to know their answer to it.

journey.section: Paying in Australian dollars or another currency
journey.quote: A quote in Australian dollars lets you compare like with like.
journey.reaction: Currency surprises are a real fear for us with a European wedding and honeymoon. Glad they address it plainly.
Sensible, but this section reads like a government checklist I could get from Smartraveller. I skimmed it. It's drifting from what a planner costs.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Honeymoon planning with us follows the same Wedded Advisor process as Wedded Concierge, whether the honeymoon follows a destination wedding or stands on its own.
journey.reaction: This is the line that matters for us. Same person for the wedding and the honeymoon. But it doesn't say whether the honeymoon is a separate fee from the wedding planning or folded in.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: One person stays with you to the end, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One accountable person is exactly what I want, and it eases the 'outsourced to strangers' worry. Fee in writing first is the minimum, but they've said it clearly.

journey.quote: Each planner sets their own fee, and it depends on how they charge and on the trip you want.
journey.reaction: The FAQ asks the exact question I typed and still gives no range or even the way Wedded Wonderland charges. Vague pricing is my biggest turn-off. Understand it may not be theirs to publish here, but it's the gap.

journey.quote: Tell your Wedded Advisor the shape of the trip, agree the fee in writing before any work begins, and see every inclusion on paper before you commit.
journey.reaction: Calm close, no pressure. I like that. Not enough on its own to make me enquire.

unanswered_questions: How does Wedded Wonderland charge for honeymoon planning: flat fee, percentage, commissions or a mix? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commissions from the hotels and suppliers it books, and will it disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Is there any ballpark or range for the planning fee, even a starting point? (deferred business detail)
If we use Wedded Concierge for the wedding, is the honeymoon a separate fee or part of the same engagement? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real honeymoon (destination, length, dates) you've planned that we can look at? (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks or extras for couples who plan both the wedding and honeymoon with you? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland hold insolvency insurance, since the page tells us to ask? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Honeymoon Planner Cost and What the Fee Covers
turn_offs_found.why: The headline sets up a cost and the page deliberately never gives one. I accept the reason, but the opening could own that sooner and more warmly instead of 'A number on its own tells you very little', which feels a bit like a brush-off.

would_share_with: James's parents, who are contributing: the 'How planners may charge, as questions to ask' list and 'What the fee should cover, in writing', so everyone asks the same questions
James: 'The fee and the trip are two different costs', because it's how we should read every quote

cta_reaction.quote: To start that conversation, [enquire about Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planner-cost&utm_content=secondary).
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and the one-advisor, fee-in-writing, AUD promises are what we want. But we're 14 months out with no destination, and I enquire after a couple of posts and a real wedding I can picture. This page gives me good questions but no picture of what working with them looks like or roughly what it costs. I'd save it and keep reading.

top_3_changes: Soften the intro's no-number moment: after 'A number on its own tells you very little.', say plainly and early that this guide won't quote a figure and will instead show how to get one in writing that you can trust, so it reads as a promise rather than a dodge.

In 'How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland', speak to couples planning both: after 'whether the honeymoon follows a destination wedding or stands on its own', add generic reader advice to ask whether wedding and honeymoon planning are quoted together or separately. No Wedded Wonderland fee facts needed.

Trim or tighten 'Protecting what you pay' so it stays on the planner and the fee (e.g. keep the insolvency and chargeback points, shorten the insurance detail and lean on the Smartraveller link), because it reads like a generic checklist and slows the page.

open_questions.question: Can a generic line advising couples to ask whether wedding and honeymoon planning are quoted together or separately be added without any Wedded Wonderland fee facts?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via Google for 'honeymoon planner cost' while early in destination wedding research, so relevance is 3 (honeymoon is secondary to the wedding for now) and enquiry likelihood is 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
The lack of figures, fee model and commissions is a deliberate deferral and is not penalised as a must-fix.

The 3-minute budget covered the intro, key takeaways, what you pay for, fee vs trip, the questions list, the Wedded Wonderland section, the FAQ and the close, with a skim of the protection and currency sections.
